title: Claude Prompts: Replace the Noun With Verbs, Then Assemble a Crew
description:
Claude prompts that ask for a noun get exactly that noun: ask Claude for a deck and you get a deck. Two Claude tips from Felix Rieseberg, an engineering manager at Anthropic, on his own blog: replace the noun with verbs, then assemble a crew of fields you would never think to ask for.

What you will see in this 118-second Short:
→ Range, in Felix's words: "Drawing on multiple fields rather than just the one the task might need at the surface". Now that multi-agent setups are easier to run, he has seen really interesting results asking Claude to bring in additional fields
→ Trick one, which he credits to The Art of Innovation by Tom Kelley and Jonathan Littman: replace the nouns with verbs. A quarterly review isn't "a deck", it's "getting busy people to believe a story about cause and effect, and to decide under uncertainty, in 30 minutes"
→ Trick two, assemble the crew, the way every heist movie does: the deck has to be amazing or aliens blow up Earth. For production quality an analyst, a journalist and an editor; if it has to be presented, a motion and audio designer; then a red team, a short seller and a forensic accountant
→ Where he sees the most magic: his colleague Alex Albert rendering interior designs in Blender got him thinking about Claude for 3D environments on his homepage. That homepage is a 3D room today (captured 2026-10-21)
→ The guardrail: don't ask the model to write like a short seller, ask it to do what a short seller does to research their position. Role play makes the transcript weirder without improving the outcome
→ This is Felix's personal advice on his own site, not an Anthropic policy, and he says it is not model-specific
